source.title: Three open problems in function theoretic operator theory

accepted.question_text: Let A be an n by n complex matrix. Let W(A) = {<Ax, x> : x is in C^n and ||x|| = 1} be the numerical range of A, and for a complex polynomial p let ||p(A)|| be the operator norm of p(A). Is it always true that ||p(A)|| <= 2 max{|p(z)| : z is in W(A)}? Equivalently, does the constant-2 numerical-range functional calculus bound hold for every complex matrix and every complex polynomial?

evidence.quote: The numerical range of A, also called the field of values, is denoted by W(A)
Thus, the Crouzeix conjecture was born. Conjecture 2.2 (Crouzeix's conjecture).
At the time of this writing this remains the best constant.

accepted.question_text: Let Theta be a finite Blaschke product, let K_Theta be its associated model space in the Hardy space H^2(D), and let S_Theta be the compression P_Theta M_z restricted to K_Theta of multiplication by z. Let B be another finite Blaschke product with degree(B) < degree(Theta). Must max{|B(z)| : z is in W(S_Theta)} be at least 1/2, where W(S_Theta) is the numerical range of S_Theta?

evidence.quote: Let Theta denote a degree-n finite Blaschke product
This version of Crouzeix's conjecture is sometimes referred to as the Level Set Crouzeix Conjecture.

accepted.question_text: Let A be a complex matrix whose numerical range W(A) is an elliptical disk, possibly degenerate. Does Crouzeix's inequality ||p(A)|| <= 2 max{|p(z)| : z is in W(A)} hold for every complex polynomial p?

evidence.quote: Question 2.7. Let A be a matrix with elliptical numerical range. Does Crouzeix's conjecture hold
This may be a good problem to consider next.

accepted.question_text: Let Theta be a finite Blaschke product with distinct zeros, and let S_Theta be the compression of the unilateral shift to the model space K_Theta associated with Theta. For a matrix representing S_Theta that is diagonalized as A = X D X^{-1}, what is the smallest possible condition number ||X|| ||X^{-1}|| among eigenvector matrices X?
accepted.context_brief: condition number for model-space shift compression

evidence.quote: Question 2.8. Let Theta be a finite Blaschke product with distinct zeros.
What is the minimal condition number of an eigenvector matrix X

accepted.question_text: Let p be a complex polynomial whose zeros all lie in the closed unit disk. For each zero a of p, must the closed disk {z : |z - a| <= 1} contain at least one critical point of p?

evidence.quote: The Sendov conjecture says that every disk of radius one centered at a zero
Despite important work, the conjecture remains open for polynomials of degree n

accepted.question_text: Let p(z) = product_{k=1}^n (z - z_k) be a complex polynomial of degree n >= 2. Define sigma_infinity(p) = min_{c in C} max_{1 <= k <= n} |z_k - c|, the radius of the smallest closed disk containing all zeros of p. If zeta is any point in the convex hull of the zeros z_1, ..., z_n, must the closed disk centered at zeta with radius sigma_infinity(p) contain a critical point of p?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.3 (Schmeisser's conjecture). Let p be a polynomial of degree n >= 2
Then the closed disk centered at zeta with radius sigma_infinity(p) contains a critical point

accepted.question_text: Let A be an n by n normal matrix. Let W(A) be its numerical range, sigma(A) its spectrum, and for each k let A_k be the (n - 1) by (n - 1) matrix obtained from A by deleting the kth row and kth column. Let H denote Hausdorff distance between compact subsets of the complex plane. Is max_{1 <= k <= n} H(W(A), sigma(A_k)) <= min_{c in C} ||A - cI||?

accepted.question_text: Let X be an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space and let T be a bounded linear operator on X. Is it true that T must have a nontrivial invariant subspace, meaning a closed subspace M with M not equal to {0} or X and T(M) contained in M? The source records this broad Banach-space form as resolved negatively by counterexamples, including an operator on l^1 with no nontrivial invariant subspaces.

evidence.quote: Question 5.1. Let X be a complex Banach space of infinite dimension
Read discovered a counterexample in a classical Banach space

accepted.question_text: Let H be a complex separable Hilbert space of infinite dimension and let T be a bounded linear operator on H. Must T have a nontrivial invariant subspace, meaning a proper nonzero closed subspace M of H such that T(M) is contained in M?

evidence.quote: The existing results do not provide an answer to the invariant subspace problem
Every operator T in L(H) has a n.t.i.s.

accepted.question_text: Let C_+ be the right half-plane, let H^2(C_+) be the Hardy space on C_+, and let phi : C_+ -> C_+ be an affine self-map. Let C_phi be the composition operator on H^2(C_+) and C_phi^* its adjoint. Is C_phi^* - lambda I universal on H^2(C_+) for some complex scalar lambda if and only if phi is elliptic and not an automorphism? Here universal means that every bounded operator on the ambient separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is similar, up to a nonzero scalar multiple, to the restriction of the universal operator to some invariant subspace.
accepted.context_brief: universal adjoints of affine composition operators
